*** IT IS SUNDAY: EVERY FIGURE IS FRIDAY'S CLOSE EXCEPT BITCOIN ***
Equities, oil, metals, currencies and bonds were all shut on Saturday and Sunday. Bitcoin trades
continuously and is the only genuinely live value in the ticker — read at 09:06 BST and declared.

*** FRIDAY WAS SHARPLY RISK-OFF, AND LONDON AGAIN WENT THE OTHER WAY ***

Oil up nearly four per cent and the volatility index up more than a fifth in a single session is a
material move, and the obvious candidate for the cause is the escalation in the Strait of Hormuz.
The FTSE closed higher for a FOURTH consecutive session, which is verifiable from our own published
series: 10,724.86 Wednesday, 10,840.35 Thursday, 10,881.90 Friday, each read and published here.

*** TWO INSTRUMENTS WHERE THE FEED'S PREVIOUS-CLOSE FIELD IS SELF-REFERENTIAL AND THE CHANGE HAD TO BE
    COMPUTED BY HAND — DECLARED, BECAUSE A COMPUTED FIGURE IS NOT A PROVIDER'S FIGURE ***
  Brent: CNBC returns last 109.86, change "UNCH", previous_day_closing 109.86 — prev equals last, so
         the field is useless. The stamp also reads 2026-10-17, a Saturday, when oil does not trade;
         that is the Friday settle carried forward with a stale stamp. Computed against Thursday's
         settle of 105.92, established in Friday's own summary file: +3.72%.
         Trading Economics corroborates the MOVE at +3.51% while giving a level of 101.41 — about
         eight and a half dollars below CNBC. That is the third consecutive day its Brent page has
         returned a WTI-like level, so the level is discarded and only the direction and rough
         magnitude are taken from it. Those agree with the computation, which is what matters here.
  Gold:  CNBC returns last 4,165.01, change "UNCH", prev 4,165.007 — again self-referential, and the
         stamp of 18 Oct 01:37 EDT is a carry rather than a trade. Computed against Thursday's close
         of 4,170.245: -0.13%. Trading Economics gives -0.11%, which corroborates it.

*** WHERE THE PROVIDER'S OWN CHANGE FIGURE IS SOUND AND IS USED AS GIVEN ***
  FTSE  +0.38% against a correct prev of 10,840.35 — and Trading Economics returns 10,881.90 +0.38%,
        identical to the decimal. No ambiguity.
  S&P   -1.09% against a correct prev of 7,744.06, which is the Thursday close we published.
  VIX   +21.45% against a correct prev of 16.46, the Thursday close we published.
  GBP   +0.41% and EURGBP -0.21% — prev equals last on both, but the change_pct field carries Friday's
        move and is used.
  UST   5.081 against a prev of 5.087, a fall of 0.006 -> published 5.08, -0.01.
  Gilt  5.3771 against a prev of 5.3765, a rise of 0.0006 -> published 5.38, +0.00. Trading Economics
        gives 5.38 with a change of 0.001. Both say flat; the gilt has now been flat to the nearest
        basis point for two consecutive readings, Friday morning and Friday's close.
